bull.b: The current absence of debt reduces mandatory financing costs and refinancing exposure while preserving flexibility to fund clinical development. Positive TTM equity also provides a stronger capital base than the company had in 2025, although continued losses could weaken it again.

The substantial financing provides resources to continue research, clinical programs, and integration of the acquired Orphai business over the coming quarters. This improves near-term funding capacity compared with relying solely on repeated equity raises, even though future warrant exercise is uncertain.

Divesting the Italian subsidiary and associated EryDex assets narrows the company’s portfolio and removes related infrastructure from the balance sheet. A more focused strategy can concentrate capital and management attention on remaining priorities, while the transaction also modestly increases cash.

bear.b: Quince has not yet demonstrated a commercial revenue engine, so its ability to fund operations depends on advancing candidates toward approval, partnerships, or future commercialization. Until then, operating scale and financial durability remain unproven and highly dependent on capital access.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means the company consumes substantial cash while its programs remain in development. The widening TTM loss increases the amount of capital required to sustain operations, raising the likelihood of additional financing and pressure on shareholder capital.

The Nasdaq notice creates an ongoing listing risk that could complicate access to public capital and increase uncertainty around the company’s trading venue. Management is evaluating a move to the Capital Market, but restoration of compliance and continued listing are not assured.
